questions.stem: A 20 year old woman has a 2 day history of sore throat, runny nose and a dry cough. Her temperature is 37.6°C, pulse rate 82 bpm and BP 116/74 mmHg. Both palatine tonsils are red and mildly enlarged with no exudate. There is no cervical lymphadenopathy and no splenomegaly.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Red tonsils with cough, coryza, low fever and no exudate is viral tonsillitis, the commonest cause.

clues: runny nose and a dry cough
steps.x: **Cough**, **coryza**, low fever, **no exudate**.

elim: No exudate, low fever and a cough make a bacterial cause unlikely.
Drooling, stridor and a toxic patient.
Needs marked lymphadenopathy, exudate and often splenomegaly.

steps.x: **E. Viral tonsillitis.** Most tonsillitis is viral; cough and coryza point away from strep.

questions.stem: A 19 year old university student has a 2 day history of severe sore throat and painful swallowing. Two of her flatmates had a similar illness last week. Her temperature is 38.5°C, pulse rate 98 bpm. Both tonsils are enlarged with white exudate and there are tender anterior cervical lymph nodes.
questions.q: Which feature of her history most increases the likelihood of this condition?
o: Use of the oral contraceptive pill
questions.e: Tonsillitis is commonest in children and young adults and is associated with contact with infected individuals.

clues: Two of her flatmates had a similar illness
steps.x: Young adult in **close contact** with cases.
**A. Contact with infected flatmates.** Risk: young age and contact with infected people.

questions.stem: A 24 year old man has a 3 day history of sore throat and painful swallowing. He has no cough. His temperature is 38.6°C, pulse rate 102 bpm and BP 124/78 mmHg. Both tonsils are swollen and covered with white exudate, and there are tender anterior cervical lymph nodes.
questions.q: What is his Centor score?
questions.e: Exudate, tender anterior nodes, fever above 38°C and absence of cough: all four Centor criteria.

steps.x: Count: **exudate**, **nodes**, **fever >38°C**, **no cough**.
**E. 4.** Centor score 4: high probability of group A strep.

questions.stem: A 31 year old woman has a 2 day history of sore throat with a productive cough and runny nose. Her temperature is 37.7°C and pulse rate 84 bpm. Both tonsils have white exudate. There is no cervical lymphadenopathy.
questions.q: What is her Centor score?
questions.e: Only tonsillar exudate scores; cough is present, fever is under 38°C and there are no tender anterior nodes.

steps.x: Only **exudate** counts here.

elim: Cough is present and nodes are absent.

steps.x: **B. 1.** Fever must be above 38°C and cough must be absent to score.

questions.stem: A 16 year old boy has a 3 day history of a severe sore throat, fever and painful swallowing. He has no cough. His temperature is 38.8°C, pulse rate 104 bpm and BP 118/70 mmHg. His GP suspects group A streptococcal tonsillitis and examines his throat.
questions.q: Which is the most likely finding on examination of the throat?
o: Grey membrane that bleeds when removed
questions.e: Bacterial tonsillitis gives enlarged hyperaemic tonsils with white exudate and tender anterior cervical nodes.

steps.x: Strep throat: tonsils covered in **pus**.

elim: Epiglottitis, seen on airway assessment, not on routine throat exam.

steps.x: **B. Enlarged tonsils with white exudate.** Exam: enlarged tonsils with white exudate.

questions.stem: A 27 year old man has had tonsillitis for 5 days. His throat pain is now much worse on the left, he is drooling and his breath smells foul. His temperature is 38.9°C and pulse rate 110 bpm. His voice is muffled and he can open his mouth only two fingers' width.
questions.q: Which is the most likely finding on examination of the oropharynx?
o: Tender swelling above and lateral to the left tonsil
questions.e: Quinsy is pus between the tonsillar capsule and pharyngeal muscles, giving a tender peritonsillar mass, trismus, hot potato voice and foul breath.

steps.x: One-sided pain, **trismus**, muffled voice, **foul breath**: quinsy.

elim: Uncomplicated tonsillitis does not cause trismus or a one-sided picture.
Peritonsillar pus produces a visible mass.

steps.x: **E. Tender swelling above and lateral to the left tonsil.** Quinsy: tender peritonsillar mass.

questions.stem: A 10 year old girl had a sore throat with fever 3 weeks ago that was not treated. She now has fever, painful swelling moving from her right knee to her left ankle, and a new pansystolic murmur. Her temperature is 38.2°C and pulse rate 118 bpm. Her ESR is raised.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Migratory polyarthritis and carditis weeks after untreated group A strep tonsillitis is rheumatic fever.

clues: 3 weeks ago that was not treated
moving from her right knee to her left ankle
steps.x: **Weeks after** untreated strep: **migratory** joints + **carditis**.

elim: Purpuric rash and abdominal pain, no carditis.
No predisposing valve lesion; migratory arthritis weeks after sore throat suggests rheumatic fever.
Not migratory and not linked to a recent sore throat with carditis.
A single hot joint, not migratory polyarthritis with carditis.

steps.x: **D. Rheumatic fever.** Rheumatic fever: delayed complication of untreated GAS.

questions.stem: A 9 year old boy had untreated tonsillitis with exudate and fever 2 weeks ago. He now has puffy eyes and dark, cola-coloured urine. His BP is 138/90 mmHg, pulse rate 92 bpm and temperature 37.0°C. Urine dipstick shows blood 3+ and protein 1+.
questions.q: Which is the most likely complication?
questions.e: Haematuria, oedema and hypertension 2 weeks after untreated group A strep is post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.

steps.x: **Two weeks** after strep: nephritic picture.

elim: Haematuria 1 to 2 days after infection, not 2 weeks.
Heavy proteinuria and oedema without haematuria or hypertension.
Affects joints and heart, not kidneys.
Gives dysuria and nitrites, not hypertension and oedema.

steps.x: **C. Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.** PSGN occurs weeks after untreated GAS (IgA nephropathy is days).

questions.stem: A 22 year old woman has had a sore throat for 4 days and was started on antibiotics yesterday. She returns to the GP feeling worse. Her temperature is 38.7°C and pulse rate 104 bpm. The GP is concerned about a peritonsillar abscess.
questions.q: Which additional feature would most support this concern?
questions.e: Trismus, muffled voice and severe one-sided throat pain are emergency features suggesting quinsy.

steps.x: Quinsy signs: **trismus**, hot potato voice, unilateral severe pain.

elim: Present in tonsillitis of any kind.
A Centor feature, not specific to quinsy.

steps.x: **E. Trismus.** Trismus = quinsy until proven otherwise.

questions.stem: A 15 year old girl has a 3 day history of severe sore throat, fever and no cough. Her temperature is 38.9°C. Both tonsils have exudate and she has tender anterior cervical nodes. A throat swab is sent and plated on blood agar.
questions.q: Which is the most likely result of the throat swab culture?
questions.e: A throat swab confirms group A strep (Streptococcus pyogenes), a beta-haemolytic Gram-positive coccus in chains.

steps.x: Centor 4: expect **group A strep**.

elim: Streptococcus pneumoniae, not a cause of tonsillitis.

steps.x: **B. Beta-haemolytic Gram-positive cocci in chains.** Throat swab confirms GAS when bacterial infection is suspected.

questions.stem: A 21 year old man has a 2 day history of severe sore throat, painful swallowing and fever. He has no cough. His temperature is 38.7°C and pulse rate 106 bpm. Both tonsils have pus on them and there are tender anterior cervical nodes.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Fever, exudate and no cough with neutrophilia and a raised CRP points to bacterial tonsillitis.

steps.x: Centor 4 and **raised WCC and CRP**: bacterial.

elim: Gives a lymphocytosis with atypical lymphocytes, not neutrophilia.
White plaques in an immunocompromised patient, no high fever.
Neutrophilia and a high CRP point to bacteria.

steps.x: **A. Bacterial tonsillitis.** Bacterial tonsillitis may show raised WCC and CRP.

questions.stem: A 6 year old girl has a 2 day history of fever, headache and malaise. She is refusing food because swallowing hurts but is drinking. Her temperature is 38.4°C, pulse rate 118 bpm and respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute. Both tonsils are enlarged with exudate. There is no rash, drooling or stridor.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Fever, odynophagia, headache and malaise with exudative tonsils in a child is tonsillitis.

clues: Both tonsils are enlarged with exudate
steps.x: Child with **odynophagia** and **exudative tonsils**, no airway signs.

elim: Oral ulcers and vesicles on hands and feet.
Fever over 5 days with conjunctivitis, rash and cracked lips.

steps.x: **E. Tonsillitis.** Commonest in children and young adults.

questions.stem: A 29 year old woman has a 2 day history of sore throat, sneezing and a cough. Her temperature is 37.5°C, pulse rate 78 bpm and BP 112/70 mmHg. Her tonsils are mildly red with no exudate and there are no tender nodes. She is eating and drinking.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation?
questions.e: Tonsillitis is a clinical diagnosis; a throat swab is only sent if bacterial infection is suspected.

steps.x: Centor **0**: clinical diagnosis, no swab.

elim: Does not change management in a mild viral illness.
No lymphadenopathy, exudate or splenomegaly to suggest glandular fever.
For suspected bacterial infection; her Centor score is 0.

steps.x: **D. No investigation required.** Clinical diagnosis; swab only if bacterial suspected.

questions.stem: A 13 year old boy has a 2 day history of sore throat and fever. His temperature is 38.3°C. On examination the lymphoid masses between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches are enlarged and red. A student asks which tissue is inflamed.
questions.q: Which structure is primarily affected?
questions.e: Tonsillitis is inflammation of the palatine tonsils, lymphoid tissue forming part of Waldeyer's ring.

clues: between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches
steps.x: Between the **arches**: the **palatine** tonsils.

elim: Lie in the nasopharynx, not between the arches.
A laryngeal cartilage, not lymphoid tissue.
Lies at the base of the tongue.

steps.x: **D. Palatine tonsils of Waldeyer's ring.** Palatine tonsils are part of Waldeyer's ring.

questions.stem: A 12 year old boy has migratory joint pains and a new murmur. His mother says he had a sore throat 4 weeks ago that was not seen by a doctor. His temperature is 38.0°C and pulse rate 112 bpm. The team wants evidence of a recent group A streptococcal infection.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation?
questions.e: Streptolysin O is a GAS virulence factor; a raised ASO titre shows recent infection when the swab may now be negative.

clues: evidence of a recent group A streptococcal infection
steps.x: Infection was **weeks ago**: look for **antibodies** to a strep toxin.

elim: Screens for kidney involvement but does not show prior strep.

steps.x: **A. Anti-streptolysin O titre.** ASO titre shows recent GAS infection.

questions.stem: A 25 year old woman has a 3 day history of sore throat with fever and no cough. Her temperature is 38.6°C, pulse rate 100 bpm. Both tonsils have exudate and she has tender anterior cervical nodes. She had anaphylaxis to penicillin as a child. She takes no other medication.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate management?
questions.e: Centor 4 needs antibiotics; with penicillin allergy clarithromycin is used (alternatives erythromycin or azithromycin).

steps.x: Centor 4 + **penicillin allergy**.
**B. Clarithromycin.** Penicillin allergic: clarithromycin.

questions.stem: A 34 year old man has a 2 day history of sore throat and a runny nose. He has a cough. His temperature is 37.4°C, pulse rate 76 bpm. His tonsils are red without exudate and he has no tender nodes. He is eating and drinking and asks for antibiotics.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate management?
o: Paracetamol and ibuprofen with self-care advice
questions.e: Mild tonsillitis with a low Centor score is managed with self-care and analgesia.

steps.x: Centor **0**, well: **self-care**.

elim: Amoxicillin is avoided and his Centor score is 0.

steps.x: **D. Paracetamol and ibuprofen with self-care advice.** Mild cases: paracetamol and ibuprofen.

questions.stem: An 18 year old man has a 3 day history of severe sore throat. He has no cough. His temperature is 38.8°C, pulse rate 104 bpm and BP 122/76 mmHg. Both tonsils are covered in exudate and he has tender anterior cervical nodes. He is drinking well and has no allergies.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate management?
questions.e: Centor above 3: oral penicillin V for 5 to 10 days.

steps.x: Centor **4**, no allergy, drinking.

elim: He is drinking and not systemically compromised.
Not first-line; causes a rash if the cause is EBV.

steps.x: **D. Oral phenoxymethylpenicillin for 5 to 10 days.** Centor >3: phenoxymethylpenicillin.

questions.stem: A 3 year old boy has a sore throat, cough and runny nose. For 2 days he has refused almost all drinks and has had one wet nappy today. His temperature is 38.3°C, pulse rate 150 bpm and capillary refill time 4 seconds. He is lethargic. His tonsils are red without exudate.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate next step in management?
questions.e: A systemically unwell, dehydrated child unable to drink for about 2 days needs immediate admission, whatever the Centor score.

steps.x: **Dehydrated** and **lethargic**: Centor does not matter.

elim: The Centor score is irrelevant in a systemically unwell child.
He is too unwell and dehydrated for home treatment.
Unsafe in a dehydrated, lethargic child.

steps.x: **A. Admit to hospital immediately.** Systemically unwell child: admit.

questions.stem: A 26 year old man has a right peritonsillar abscess. He has trismus, a hot potato voice and drooling. His temperature is 38.8°C, pulse rate 108 bpm. The ENT team performs needle aspiration of pus and starts intravenous benzylpenicillin and metronidazole.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate adjunct treatment?
questions.e: Quinsy is treated with drainage plus antibiotics, with corticosteroids as an adjunct to reduce swelling and pain.

steps.x: Drainage and antibiotics done: add a **steroid**.

elim: Not first-line; drainage and antibiotics are.
For croup or airway oedema, not quinsy.
He is already on IV antibiotics.

steps.x: **C. Intravenous dexamethasone.** Quinsy: drainage + antibiotics, steroids as adjunct.

questions.stem: A 15 year old girl has had 8 episodes of tonsillitis in the last 12 months, each confirmed by her GP and causing her to miss school. She is currently well. Her temperature is 36.8°C. Her tonsils are mildly enlarged with no exudate.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate next step in management?
o: Wait to see if 7 more episodes occur next year
questions.e: SIGN criteria for tonsillectomy: 7 or more episodes in the preceding 12 months, 5 or more in each of 2 years, or 3 or more in each of 3 years.

clues: 8 episodes of tonsillitis in the last 12 months
steps.x: **8 in 12 months**: meets the **7+** criterion.

elim: She is well; it adds nothing.
She already meets the 7 in 12 months criterion.

steps.x: **C. Refer for tonsillectomy.** SIGN: 7+ in 1 year, 5+ in each of 2 years, 3+ in each of 3 years.

questions.stem: A 20 year old man has had 4 episodes of tonsillitis in each of the last 2 years, each managed by his GP. He asks about having his tonsils removed. He is currently well. His temperature is 36.7°C and his tonsils look normal.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate management?
o: Continue episodic treatment as he does not meet criteria
questions.e: Four episodes in each of 2 years falls short of the SIGN criterion of 5 or more in each of 2 years.

clues: 4 episodes of tonsillitis in each of the last 2 years
steps.x: **4 per year for 2 years**: needs **5+**.

elim: He does not meet SIGN criteria.
Needs 5 or more in each of 2 years; he has 4.

steps.x: **A. Continue episodic treatment as he does not meet criteria.** Tonsillectomy only if SIGN criteria are met.

questions.stem: A 23 year old woman has had 3 episodes of tonsillitis in each of the last 3 years, each causing her to take time off work. She is well today. Her temperature is 36.9°C. Her tonsils are mildly enlarged without exudate.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate next step in management?
o: Advise that she needs 7 episodes in a year
questions.e: Three or more episodes in each of the preceding 3 years meets SIGN criteria for tonsillectomy.

clues: 3 episodes of tonsillitis in each of the last 3 years
steps.x: **3+ for 3 years** meets SIGN.

elim: She meets the 3 or more in each of 3 years criterion.

steps.x: **D. Refer for tonsillectomy.** SIGN: 7 / 5+5 / 3+3+3.

questions.stem: A 67 year old man with a penicillin allergy was prescribed clarithromycin for tonsillitis 5 days ago. He also takes atorvastatin 80 mg daily. He now has aching weakness in his thighs and dark urine. His temperature is 37.2°C. Creatine kinase is markedly raised.
questions.q: Which is the most likely cause of his new symptoms?
questions.e: Clarithromycin inhibits statin metabolism, raising rhabdomyolysis risk; the statin should be held while on clarithromycin.

steps.x: Macrolide + statin, then **myalgia**, **dark urine**, **high CK**.

elim: Ascending weakness with areflexia, normal CK.
Shoulder and hip girdle stiffness with normal CK.
Haematuria but not muscle pain with a high CK.
Less likely than a known drug interaction.

steps.x: **B. Interaction between clarithromycin and atorvastatin.** Clarithromycin + atorvastatin = rhabdomyolysis risk; hold the statin.

questions.stem: A 17 year old girl with a high fever and tonsils covered in thick exudate has a throat swab that grows group A Streptococcus. Her friend with a viral sore throat had only mild fever and red tonsils. A student asks why the bacterial illness looks more inflamed.
questions.q: Which is the most likely explanation?
o: Bacteria invade the bloodstream in all cases
Streptococcal virulence factors such as M protein provoke strong inflammation
questions.e: GAS virulence factors (streptolysin O, M protein) provoke a strong inflammatory response, explaining higher fever and exudate than viral tonsillitis.

steps.x: Bacterial **toxins and surface proteins** drive inflammation.

elim: Viruses are the commonest cause of tonsillitis.

steps.x: **D. Streptococcal virulence factors such as M protein provoke strong inflammation.** Streptolysin O and M protein cause the exudative picture.

questions.stem: A GP sees a 22 year old woman with a sore throat. Her temperature is 38.4°C, she has no cough and both tonsils have exudate. The GP uses a clinical score before deciding on treatment. A student asks why this score is used.
questions.q: Which best explains the purpose of the score?
o: It confirms the diagnosis of viral infection
It estimates the probability of group A streptococcal infection
It replaces the need to examine the throat
questions.e: The Centor criteria exploit the difference between bacterial and viral tonsillitis to estimate the probability of GAS and guide antibiotics.

clues: clinical score before deciding on treatment
steps.x: The **Centor** score: probability of **strep**.

elim: It estimates probability, it does not confirm.
It estimates strep likelihood, not complications.
Exudate and nodes are examination findings.

steps.x: **B. It estimates the probability of group A streptococcal infection.** Centor estimates GAS likelihood to guide antibiotics.

questions.stem: A 14 year old boy develops a new mitral regurgitant murmur and polyarthritis 3 weeks after an untreated streptococcal sore throat. A student asks why the heart is damaged when the bacteria never reached it.
questions.q: Which is the most likely mechanism?
o: Antibodies against streptococcal M protein cross-react with cardiac tissue
Direct bacterial invasion of the valve
Immune complex deposition in the valve
Streptococcal toxin acting directly on myocardium
questions.e: Rheumatic fever is due to molecular mimicry: antibodies to streptococcal antigens attack similar human proteins in heart and joints.

clues: 3 weeks after an untreated streptococcal sore throat
steps.x: Delayed, sterile damage: **molecular mimicry**.

elim: That is infective endocarditis; no bacteria are on the valve.

steps.x: **A. Antibodies against streptococcal M protein cross-react with cardiac tissue.** Molecular mimicry between strep antigens and human tissue.

questions.stem: A 28 year old woman with tonsillitis for 6 days develops worsening left throat pain, trismus and a muffled voice. Her temperature is 38.9°C. CT neck shows a collection lateral to the left tonsil, outside its capsule, next to the pharyngeal muscles.
questions.q: Which is the most likely mechanism of this complication?
o: Lymph node necrosis in the neck
Retrograde spread from the middle ear
Spread of infection beyond the tonsillar capsule
questions.e: Infection spreads beyond the tonsillar capsule into the peritonsillar space; inflammation of the nearby pterygoid muscles causes trismus.

steps.x: Pus **outside the capsule**: spread to the peritonsillar space.

elim: The collection is peritonsillar, not in a node.

steps.x: **E. Spread of infection beyond the tonsillar capsule.** Quinsy: spread beyond the capsule; trismus from pterygoid spasm.
